title: A Natural Representation of Volumes Yields a Remarkable Affine Consequence
summary: At the beginning of the 20th Century there was a growing interest for the investigation of the action of linear groups on the geometry of surfaces. In that context of ideas, the quest for a connection between curvature and the behaviour of linear groups rose naturally. Pursuing the original thought, we investigate how the geometric meaning of this idea is intimately related to the concept of volume of parallelepiped boxes.
